Q192.reason: The friend intended to frustrate the burglary by having the young man arrested, so he lacked the intent that the crime succeed needed for conspiracy or accomplice liability.

Q193.reason: Under Plyler v. Doe, a fee that effectively excludes children from public school is not substantially related to an important governmental interest, so the ordinance is invalid.

Q194.reason: Accepting and paying for 490 widgets does not excuse non-delivery of the other 10, so the buyer can recover damages for that failure to perform.
